trivia: It was a duet from its very first recording, with Annie de Reuver and Karel van der Velden joined by The Skymasters.

title: Daar bij de waterkant
trivia: Black and White were Jan Klumperman and Eugen Gaiser from Delft, who met on a cycling holiday. Readers of Tuney Tunes voted them the best Dutch vocal group in 1955 and 1956.
notes: Came out in 1954 as the B-side of Zeep en soda (nl.wikipedia).

title: Twee motten
trivia: Dorus was the stage persona of Tom Manders, who co-wrote the song with Cor Steyn. After going viral on TikTok in 2023 it reached its highest ever place in the Radio 2 Top 2000.
notes: Single on Decca (M 64104), B-side De Nachtwacht.

title: 'n Beetje
trivia: It won the Eurovision Song Contest for the Netherlands with 21 points. The first, orchestral arrangement sold poorly, so a livelier big-band version was recorded.

track.title: 'n Beetje
track.notes: Hitster NL spells it Een Beetje; the song's own title is 'n Beetje.

notes: Exact release date not given; categorised as a 1959 single on Philips (nl.wikipedia). Music by Dick Schallies, words by Willy van Hemert.

title: Kom van dat dak af
trivia: The title means "get off that roof". Peter Koelewijn is afraid of heights and disliked the promo films that kept putting the band up on one.

track.title: Kom van dat dak af
track.notes: Credited on the single as Peter en zijn Rockets.

notes: Single 8 Jan 1960 on Imperial (recorded 1959); credited on release to Peter en zijn Rockets.

title: Marieke
trivia: Brel mixes French and Dutch in this song, which he also recorded in a fully Dutch version. A statue of Marieke by Jef Claerhout honours it.

trivia: A Philips EP pairing it with "Trommel van Bahia" reportedly stayed at number one in the Netherlands for thirteen weeks. It is a Dutch version of a German hit.

title: Ritme van de regen
trivia: Gerrit den Braber wrote the Dutch words under the pseudonym Lodewijk Post. Producer Jan de Winter was unhappy with the first session, and the take used on the record was finished within an hour on the second.

track.title: Ritme van de regen
track.notes: Rob de Nijs's Dutch version, not The Cascades original.

trivia: Corry Brokken sang this Dutch version of a Charles Aznavour song. She was also a trained lawyer.

notes: Dutch-language cover of Aznavour's La Mamma, kept as the famous Dutch version. Year 1964 from the Top 2000 list snippet on nl.wikipedia; exact release not found.

title: Een meisje van zestien
trivia: It is a Dutch version of Charles Aznavour's "Une enfant", with words by Lennaert Nijgh. It was Boudewijn de Groot's first hit.

title: Ben ik te min
trivia: It began as the B-side of Armand's second single and only took off after Radio Veronica played it, reaching number five in the Veronica Top 40.
notes: Single 7 Nov 1966 on Fontana (nl.wikipedia); written by Armand (Herman van Loenhout).

title: Welterusten meneer de president
trivia: Boudewijn de Groot wanted to write something about the Vietnam War, and lyricist Lennaert Nijgh turned it into an appeal to US president Lyndon B. Johnson.
notes: Single 4 Apr 1966 on Decca; also on his debut album. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Ik ben gelukkig zonder jou
trivia: Peter Koelewijn and Hanny Meijler wrote this song about divorce, which was seen as an emblem of the women's movement of the day. It was Conny Vandenbos's first hit.
notes: Year 1966 from the Top 2000 list and the Daisy a Day article; peaked at number 9 in the Top 40. nl.wikipedia mentions no 1974 re-release or re-recording. Hitster NL list shows 1974; card uses 1966.

title: Sure He's a Cat
trivia: The Cats came from Volendam, the fishing town behind the palingsound. This single reached number twelve in the Dutch Top 40.
notes: Single 1967; the band's first LP Cats as Cats Can is also 1967.

title: Window of My Eyes
trivia: It reached number ten in the Dutch Top 40 and has charted in the NPO Radio 2 Top 2000 in most years since the list began.
notes: Single released 1968 (28 Sep 1968 chart entry, number 10 in the Top 40 and Parool Top 20) per the Cuby + Blizzards discography on nl.wikipedia. Album not stated. Hitster NL list shows 1967; card uses 1968.

title: Hair
trivia: Zen's version of the title song of the musical Hair held number one in the Dutch charts for three weeks in early 1969.

track.title: Hair

title: Venus
trivia: Guitarist Robbie van Leeuwen wrote it over the tune of an earlier folk song, "The Banjo Song". It became the first song by a Dutch group to top the US Hot 100.
notes: Netherlands single 14 Jul 1969; the 1969 album At Home gained Venus only as a bonus track on its 1989 CD reissue. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Ma Belle Amie
trivia: American producer Jerry Ross heard it in a Swiss club and signed the band, after which it reached number five on the US Hot 100.
notes: Netherlands single July 1969 (Tee Set Records); written by Peter Tetteroo and Hans van Eijck. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Hocus Pocus
trivia: Thijs van Leer's flute and wordless yodelling vocals, plus Jan Akkerman's guitar riff, give it its unmistakable hook.
notes: First released as a single in 1971; album Moving Waves also 1971 (nl.wikipedia snippet). Chart success in the UK and US came later. Album version 6:41; the single edit is shorter. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: How Do You Do!
trivia: It sold over a million copies worldwide and earned its makers the 1972 Conamus Export Prize.
notes: Sources conflict. Harry van Hoof's nl.wikipedia entry calls the song from 1971, Willem Duyn's entry says it was an international hit in 1972, and a chart entry following a number one that ended in Dec 1971 points to a late 1971 release. Card uses 1971; use 1972 if the hit year is preferred. Written by Hans van Hemert and Harry van Hoof. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: 1948 (Toen was geluk heel gewoon)

track.title: 1948 (Toen was geluk heel gewoon)
track.notes: Gerard Cox's Dutch version, not O'Sullivan's original.

title: Radar Love
trivia: It came out in the Netherlands first, reached the UK a couple of months later and only arrived in the US the following spring.
notes: Dutch single Aug 1973, UK Oct 1973, US Apr 1974; album Moontan 1973. Album version 6:26, single edit 5:04.

title: Het dorp

title: Una Paloma Blanca
trivia: It sold more than a million copies and earned the group a Buma Export Prize.
notes: Single released March 1975 per the Paloma Blanca snippet on nl.wikipedia. Hitster NL credits George Baker and George Baker Selection.

title: Mississippi
trivia: Pussycat, from Limburg, topped the charts in several countries including the UK and Germany. Werner Theunissen wrote the song.
notes: Single April 1975 per en.wikipedia. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

notes: Single 1975 on Philips; music by Dick Bakker, words by Will Luikinga and Eddy Ouwens. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

notes: Release linked to November 1979 on nl.wikipedia snippets; exact day not given.

trivia: Joost Timp wrote it with Will Hoebee producing. The first single from the album of the same name sold roughly 45,000 copies, a big success.

title: Why Tell Me Why
trivia: Piet Souer composed it. It topped the Dutch charts for several weeks, and a 2011 remix by Guilliano made it a hit again.
notes: Dutch Top 40 run began early Oct 1981 (nl.wikipedia snippet); album not verified.

notes: Single 1981, track A1 of Skunk; written by Henny Vrienten. B-sides Het leven gaat door and Er verandert niks. The opening line of the nl.wikipedia article gives the full title. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Twilight Zone

notes: Single 23 Aug 1982; album Cut 1982. Album version 7:58, single edit 4:47. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: 1 nacht alleen
trivia: Henny Vrienten wrote and sang it. It comes from 4us, the band's fourth studio album, made shortly before they split up.
notes: Single 1983; album 4us recorded late 1982.

title: Annabel

notes: Hans de Booij single June 1983. Not verified whether Boudewijn de Groot released his own version earlier.

title: Als je wint

notes: Appears in the list of Alarmschijven of January 1984 and in the 1984 Top 2000 list (nl.wikipedia snippets).

notes: Single 1985 on WEA; Dutch Top 40 number one 26 Oct to 1 Nov 1985 (nl.wikipedia). Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Anne
trivia: Herman van Veen wrote it about his daughter Anne and recorded it in both Dutch and German.

notes: Album released 16 Sep 1987 per nl.wikipedia snippet; single followed in 1987.

notes: Album Hoezo? came out in Oct 1989 and the single followed in Jan 1990 (nl.wikipedia snippets). Album-first rule gives 1989; Hitster NL shows 1990. Belgian band so region be. Hitster NL list shows 1990; card uses 1989.

title: Smoorverliefd
trivia: Snelle made it for an Interpolis campaign warning against using a phone while cycling. It was streamed more than 460,000 times on the day after release, a personal record for him.
notes: Single 10 Jan 2020; album Lars followed in 2021. Number one in the Dutch Top 40 and Single Top 100. Written by Lars Bos (Snelle) and Okke Punt.

title: Europapa
trivia: Joost Klein's Eurovision entry for the Netherlands was the most streamed song of the 2024 field on Spotify and YouTube, even though he was removed from the contest before the final.
notes: Released 29 Feb 2024 after a premiere on De Avondshow met Arjen Lubach; number one on the Dutch Top 40 and Single Top 100. Credited on streaming as Joost. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.
